notice: Rule-based pattern analysis on this machine. Rules miss things and can be wrong; no detection rate is claimed. No findings means no rule fired, not that the code is secure.

findings.message: Possible github token hard-coded in the file (github_token:ghp_…).
findings.why: A GitHub token grants access to repositories and actions under its owner's account.
findings.fix: Revoke the token in GitHub settings, then read a new one from the environment or your CI secrets.

findings.message: subprocess.run runs a built command through the shell (shell=True).
findings.why: With shell=True the command is parsed by /bin/sh. Any interpolated value can add ';', '&&' or '$(...)' and run other commands.
findings.fix: Pass the command as a list of arguments without shell=True, for example subprocess.run(['git', 'log', ref], check=True). Use shlex.quote only when a shell is unavoidable.

findings.message: eval() runs a value that is not a literal as code.
findings.why: eval runs its argument as Python code. If any part of it comes from a user, a file or the network, an attacker can run arbitrary code.
findings.fix: Parse data instead of evaluating it: ast.literal_eval for Python literals, json.loads for JSON, or an explicit lookup table.

findings.why: MD5 and SHA-1 have practical collision attacks and must not protect integrity, signatures or passwords.
findings.fix: Use hashlib.sha256 (or hashlib.blake2b). For passwords use a slow KDF such as hashlib.scrypt. If the hash is only a checksum or an identifier, pass usedforsecurity=False.
